---
title: "Airform"
description: "dbt-style, version-controlled SQL modeling for Oxygen"
---

**Airform** is Oxygen's modeling engine. It turns raw tables into clean,
tested ones with dbt-style SQL models that live in the same workspace as your
agents and semantic model, so the tables your metrics build on are defined in
code rather than assembled ad hoc. It works in three stages:

- **Compile** resolves each model into plain SQL and works out the
  dependencies between models.
- **Build** runs that SQL on the warehouse in dependency order.
- **Test** checks the tables it built.

<Frame caption="Airform compiles a dbt-style project into plain SQL, builds the models in dependency order on your warehouse, and tests the tables the semantic model relies on.">

## Why it matters

- **Transforms are code.** Models are reviewed and deployed through the same
  Git flow as the rest of the workspace.
- **Tested foundations.** Every model can carry tests, so the semantic model
  compiles over tables that are checked, not assumed.
- **Readable and traceable.** Every model compiles to plain SQL you can read
  before it runs, with model- and column-level lineage across the project.
- **No separate tool.** Airform follows dbt conventions, so existing projects
  carry over with one added mapping file, and without a separate dbt
  installation or Python environment.

## Where it fits

Airform builds models on the warehouses already connected to the workspace,
including Snowflake, BigQuery, Postgres, Redshift, and DuckDB, and its output
is what the [semantic model](/guide/build/semantic-model/simple-model) defines
measures over.
